# Spec: data-model-seed

## Goal
Add the P0 data model, the first Alembic migration and a demo seed command (build step 2, `design/DESIGN.md:65`).
The schema enforces tenant isolation for writes with composite foreign keys. The seed data shows the matcher trade-offs that later steps demonstrate.

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | The tests must prove |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | `uv run alembic upgrade head` on an empty database creates the 8 tables and the 4 native enum types. (DESIGN Data model, `design/DESIGN.md:121-232`) | After the upgrade, the tables `organization`, `app_user`, `skill`, `crew_skill`, `unavailability`, `mission`, `mission_requirement`, `assignment` exist. The enum types `user_role`, `mission_status`, `assignment_status`, `unavailability_reason` exist with the values of the design. |
| AC2 | The migration and the models agree, and the downgrade is complete. | `alembic check` reports no difference. A downgrade to `base` removes all 8 tables and all 4 enum types. A second upgrade then succeeds. |
| AC3 | Each tenant table has `org_id NOT NULL`. The DB rejects each cross-org link of the composite foreign key table. (P0 req 4, `design/DESIGN.md:357-371`) | For each row of `design/DESIGN.md:363-371`, an insert that links rows of two different orgs fails with an integrity error. The same insert with rows of one org succeeds. An insert with `org_id` NULL fails. |
| AC4 | An assignment can reference only a slot of its own mission. (`design/DESIGN.md:225`) | An assignment with `mission_id` of mission A and `requirement_id` of a slot of mission B in the same org fails. |
| AC5 | The DB enforces the value checks. (`design/DESIGN.md:169`, `:182`, `:196`, `:211`) | `crew_skill.level` and `mission_requirement.min_level` reject 0 and 6, and accept 1 and 5. `unavailability` and `mission` reject `end_date` before `start_date`, and accept `end_date` equal to `start_date`. |
| AC6 | The DB enforces the unique keys. (`design/DESIGN.md:147`, `:158`, `:209`, `:230-231`) | A second user with the same `username` fails, also in another org. A second skill with the same name fails in one org and succeeds in another org. A second active slot with the same position in one mission fails. A new slot can use the position of an archived slot. A second INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment for the same mission and user fails. A second INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment for the same slot fails. A new INVITED assignment succeeds after the earlier one is DECLINED or CANCELLED. |
| AC7 | Each table has `created_at` and `updated_at`. (`design/DESIGN.md:130`) | An insert sets both values. An ORM update of a row changes `updated_at` and keeps `created_at`. |
| AC8 | `uv run mc-seed` loads the demo dataset into a migrated database. A second run gives the same state. (P0 req 1, req 3) | The command exits with 0. After two runs, the row count of each table is the same as after one run, and the usernames are the same. |
| AC9 | The seed has 2 orgs. Org A has 2 directors, 2 leads and at least 8 crew members. Org B has 1 director, 1 lead and at least 3 crew members. (P0 req 3) | The counts of users per org and role match. Each org has its own skill catalogue. At least one skill name exists in both orgs as two different rows. |
| AC10 | The seed data obeys the service rules that the DB does not enforce. (`design/DESIGN.md:172`, `:193`, `:226`, `:338-345`) | Each `crew_skill` user and each `assignment` user has the role CREW. Each mission lead has the role LEAD or DIRECTOR. Each mission with `approved_by` has an approver with the role DIRECTOR who is not the lead. Each mission in APPROVED or COMPLETED has `approved_by` and `approved_at`. Assignments exist only on missions in APPROVED or COMPLETED. No crew member has two INVITED or ACCEPTED assignments on missions with overlapping dates. Each assigned crew member has the slot skill at the minimum level or higher. |
| AC11 | The seed shows the matcher trade-offs for a reference window in org A: 2027-01-11 to 2027-01-24, slots Piloting ≥ 3, EVA ≥ 3, Medicine ≥ 2. (P0 req 3, `design/DESIGN.md:389-399`) | Expert against closest fit: two crew members have Piloting, one at level 5 and one at level 3. Leave: a crew member with EVA ≥ 3 has unavailability that overlaps the window. Booking: a crew member with Medicine ≥ 2 has an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment on a mission that overlaps the window. Workload: two crew members have EVA at the same level ≥ 3 and are free in the window. One has INVITED or ACCEPTED mission days within 60 days of the window, and the other has none. |
| AC12 | The seed has assignment history for crew members. (P0 req 14) | At least one assignment is DECLINED. At least one ACCEPTED assignment is on a COMPLETED mission. |
| AC13 | Org B has a target of each type for the cross-org checks of later steps. (P0 req 22) | Org B has at least one skill, crew skill, unavailability, mission, slot and assignment. |
| AC14 | `uv run pytest` uses a separate database `mc_test`. The dev database keeps its data. | After a full test run, the row counts in the dev database `mc` are the same as before the run. The test session creates `mc_test` if it does not exist and migrates it to `head`. |
| AC15 | The README tells the reviewer how to seed the data and which users exist. (P0 req 1) | Manual review: the README run steps contain `uv run mc-seed` after `alembic upgrade head`, and a table of the seeded usernames with org and role. |

## Non-goals
- No API endpoints and no CLI commands for the data. Steps 3 to 9 add them.
- No shared Pydantic types in `mc_shared`. No API response uses the models yet.
- No org-scoped data-access layer, no login and no JWT. Step 3 adds them.
- No matcher code. The seed only provides the data for the matcher scenarios of step 5.
- No ORM relationships between the models. A later step adds a relationship when a query needs it.
- No P1 columns: no `mission_seq`, no mission `number`, no skill `slug`.
- No docker-compose service for the seed.

## End-to-end check
| # | Action | Expected result | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Run `alembic upgrade head` on the empty `mc_test` database. | The 8 tables and the 4 enum types exist. | `packages/api/tests/test_migration.py` |
| 2 | Run `alembic downgrade base`, then `alembic upgrade head`. | Both commands succeed. No table or enum type is left after the downgrade. | `packages/api/tests/test_migration.py` |
| 3 | Run `uv run mc-seed` two times against `mc_test` as a subprocess. | Both runs exit with 0. The row counts per table are equal after each run. | `packages/api/tests/test_seed.py` |
| 4 | Query the seeded data with SQL. | The counts of AC9, the rules of AC10 and the scenarios of AC11 to AC13 are true. | `packages/api/tests/test_seed.py` |
| 5 | Read the README run steps and the user table. | The steps contain `uv run mc-seed`. The table lists each seeded username. | manual: the README content is prose. A test cannot judge that it is clear. |

## Resolved questions
| Question | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Task name and folder | `data-model-seed`, `.work/data-model-seed/` | me |
| How do the tests isolate their data? | A separate database `mc_test`. The test session creates and migrates it. Each test rolls back its transaction. | me |
| How does the reviewer load the seed? | A Python seed command `uv run mc-seed`, after `alembic upgrade head`. It deletes the existing data and inserts the seed again. | me |
| Which dates does the seed use? | Fixed dates, in the period November 2026 to March 2027. | me |
| How does the DB store the enums? | Native Postgres ENUM types. | me |
| Which values does `unavailability.reason` have? | `HOLIDAY`, `SICK`, `MEETING` only. | me |
| What is the E2E check of step 2? | An integration test runs the seed command against the test DB and checks the data with SQL. verify:full runs it with pytest. | me |
| Which build approach? | SQLAlchemy models, an autogenerated Alembic migration, a Python seed module with ORM objects. | me |
| Which table names? | `organization` and `app_user`. The other tables use the singular names of the design: `skill`, `crew_skill`, `unavailability`, `mission`, `mission_requirement`, `assignment`. | me |
| Does `crew_skill` have an `id` column? | No. The PK is `(user_id, skill_id)`. | `design/DESIGN.md:171` |
| Which values do the other enums have? | `user_role`: DIRECTOR, LEAD, CREW. `mission_status`: DRAFT, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, APPROVED, ACTIVE, COMPLETED, CANCELLED. `assignment_status`: INVITED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, CANCELLED. | `design/DESIGN.md:149`, `:194`, `:227` |
| Schema details: Python UUIDs, server default timestamps, ORM `updated_at`, naming convention, no relationships, manual enum drop in the downgrade | Approved as design section 1. | me |
| Which tables have the cross-org foreign keys? | The 7 rows of the composite foreign key table. | `design/DESIGN.md:363-371` |
| What is the workload window? | A code constant, example 90 days. The seed places the workload within 60 days of the reference window, so it counts for each window of 60 days or more. | `design/DESIGN.md:239` |
| Where is the run command? | The CLAUDE.md "Run locally" line and the README run steps. Both get the seed step. | `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md:12-18` |

# Spec: data-model-seed

## Goal
Add the P0 data model, the first Alembic migration and a demo seed command (build step 2, `design/DESIGN.md:65`).
The schema enforces tenant isolation for writes with composite foreign keys. The seed data shows the matcher trade-offs that later steps demonstrate.

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | The tests must prove |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | `uv run alembic upgrade head` on an empty database creates the 8 tables and the 4 native enum types. (DESIGN Data model, `design/DESIGN.md:121-232`) | After the upgrade, the tables `organization`, `app_user`, `skill`, `crew_skill`, `unavailability`, `mission`, `mission_requirement`, `assignment` exist. The enum types `user_role`, `mission_status`, `assignment_status`, `unavailability_reason` exist with the values of the design. |
| AC2 | The migration and the models agree, and the downgrade is complete. | `alembic check` reports no difference. A downgrade to `base` removes all 8 tables and all 4 enum types. A second upgrade then succeeds. |
| AC3 | Each tenant table has `org_id NOT NULL`. The DB rejects each cross-org link of the composite foreign key table. (P0 req 4, `design/DESIGN.md:357-371`) | For each row of `design/DESIGN.md:363-371`, an insert that links rows of two different orgs fails with an integrity error. The same insert with rows of one org succeeds. An insert with `org_id` NULL fails. |
| AC4 | An assignment can reference only a slot of its own mission. (`design/DESIGN.md:225`) | An assignment with `mission_id` of mission A and `requirement_id` of a slot of mission B in the same org fails. |
| AC5 | The DB enforces the value checks. (`design/DESIGN.md:169`, `:182`, `:196`, `:211`) | `crew_skill.level` and `mission_requirement.min_level` reject 0 and 6, and accept 1 and 5. `unavailability` and `mission` reject `end_date` before `start_date`, and accept `end_date` equal to `start_date`. |
| AC6 | The DB enforces the unique keys. (`design/DESIGN.md:147`, `:158`, `:209`, `:230-231`) | A second user with the same `username` fails, also in another org. A second skill with the same name fails in one org and succeeds in another org. A second active slot with the same position in one mission fails. A new slot can use the position of an archived slot. A second INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment for the same mission and user fails. A second INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment for the same slot fails. A new INVITED assignment succeeds after the earlier one is DECLINED or CANCELLED. |
| AC7 | Each table has `created_at` and `updated_at`. (`design/DESIGN.md:130`) | An insert sets both values. An ORM update of a row changes `updated_at` and keeps `created_at`. |

Assignments exist only on missions in APPROVED or COMPLETED. No crew member has two INVITED or ACCEPTED assignments on missions with overlapping dates. Each assigned crew member has the slot skill at the minimum level or higher. |

# Spec: data-model-seed

## Goal
Add the P0 data model, the first Alembic migration and a demo seed command (build step 2, `design/DESIGN.md:65`).
The schema enforces tenant isolation for writes with composite foreign keys. The seed data shows the matcher trade-offs that later steps demonstrate.

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | The tests must prove |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | `uv run alembic upgrade head` on an empty database creates the 8 tables and the 4 native enum types. (DESIGN Data model, `design/DESIGN.md:121-232`) | After the upgrade, the tables `organization`, `app_user`, `skill`, `crew_skill`, `unavailability`, `mission`, `mission_requirement`, `assignment` exist. The enum types `user_role`, `mission_status`, `assignment_status`, `unavailability_reason` exist with the values of the design. |
| AC2 | The migration and the models agree, and the downgrade is complete. | `alembic check` reports no difference. A downgrade to `base` removes all 8 tables and all 4 enum types. A second upgrade then succeeds. |
| AC3 | Each tenant table has `org_id NOT NULL`. The DB rejects each cross-org link of the composite foreign key table. (P0 req 4, `design/DESIGN.md:357-371`) | For each row of `design/DESIGN.md:363-371`, an insert that links rows of two different orgs fails with an integrity error. The same insert with rows of one org succeeds. An insert with `org_id` NULL fails. |
| AC4 | An assignment can reference only a slot of its own mission. (`design/DESIGN.md:225`) | An assignment with `mission_id` of mission A and `requirement_id` of a slot of mission B in the same org fails. |
| AC5 | The DB enforces the value checks. (`design/DESIGN.md:169`, `:182`, `:196`, `:211`) | `crew_skill.level` and `mission_requirement.min_level` reject 0 and 6, and accept 1 and 5. `unavailability` and `mission` reject `end_date` before `start_date`, and accept `end_date` equal to `start_date`. |
| AC6 | The DB enforces the unique keys. (`design/DESIGN.md:147`, `:158`, `:209`, `:230-231`) | A second user with the same `username` fails, also in another org. A second skill with the same name fails in one org and succeeds in another org. A second active slot with the same position in one mission fails. A new slot can use the position of an archived slot. A second INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment for the same mission and user fails. A second INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment for the same slot fails. A new INVITED assignment succeeds after the earlier one is DECLINED or CANCELLED. |
| AC7 | Each table has `created_at` and `updated_at`. (`design/DESIGN.md:130`) | An insert sets both values. An ORM update of a row changes `updated_at` and keeps `created_at`. |
| AC8 | `uv run mc-seed` loads the demo dataset into a migrated database. A second run gives the same state. (P0 req 1, req 3) | The command exits with 0. After two runs, the row count of each table is the same as after one run, and the usernames are the same. |
| AC9 | The seed has 2 orgs. Org A has 2 directors, 2 leads and at least 8 crew members. Org B has 1 director, 1 lead and at least 3 crew members. (P0 req 3) | The counts of users per org and role match. Each org has its own skill catalogue. At least one skill name exists in both orgs as two different rows. |
| AC10 | The seed data obeys the service rules that the DB does not enforce. (`design/DESIGN.md:172`, `:193`, `:226`, `:338-345`) | Each `crew_skill` user and each `assignment` user has the role CREW. Each mission lead has the role LEAD or DIRECTOR. Each mission with `approved_by` has an approver with the role DIRECTOR who is not the lead. Each mission in APPROVED or COMPLETED has `approved_by` and `approved_at`. Assignments exist only on missions in APPROVED or COMPLETED. No crew member has two INVITED or ACCEPTED assignments on missions with overlapping dates. Each assigned crew member has the slot skill at the minimum level or higher. |
| AC11 | The seed shows the matcher trade-offs for a reference window in org A: 2027-01-11 to 2027-01-24, slots Piloting ≥ 3, EVA ≥ 3, Medicine ≥ 2. (P0 req 3, `design/DESIGN.md:389-399`) | Expert against closest fit: two crew members have Piloting, one at level 5 and one at level 3. Leave: a crew member with EVA ≥ 3 has unavailability that overlaps the window. Booking: a crew member with Medicine ≥ 2 has an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment on a mission that overlaps the window. Workload: two crew members have EVA at the same level ≥ 3 and are free in the window. One has INVITED or ACCEPTED mission days within 60 days of the window, and the other has none. |
| AC12 | The seed has assignment history for crew members. (P0 req 14) | At least one assignment is DECLINED. At least one ACCEPTED assignment is on a COMPLETED mission. The COMPLETED mission ends before 2026-10-11. |
| AC13 | Org B has a target of each type for the cross-org checks of later steps. (P0 req 22) | Org B has at least one skill, crew skill, unavailability, mission, slot and assignment. |
| AC14 | `uv run pytest` uses a separate database `mc_test`. The dev database keeps its data. | After a full test run, the row counts in the dev database `mc` are the same as before the run. The test session creates `mc_test` if it does not exist and migrates it to `head`. |
| AC15 | The README tells the reviewer how to seed the data and which users exist. (P0 req 1) | Manual review: the README run steps contain `uv run mc-seed` after `alembic upgrade head`, and a table of the seeded usernames with org and role. |

## Non-goals
- No API endpoints and no CLI commands for the data. Steps 3 to 9 add them.
- No shared Pydantic types in `mc_shared`. No API response uses the models yet.
- No org-scoped data-access layer, no login and no JWT. Step 3 adds them.
- No matcher code. The seed only provides the data for the matcher scenarios of step 5.
- No ORM relationships between the models. A later step adds a relationship when a query needs it.
- No P1 columns: no `mission_seq`, no mission `number`, no skill `slug`.
- No docker-compose service for the seed.

## End-to-end check
| # | Action | Expected result | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Run `alembic upgrade head` on the empty `mc_test` database. | The 8 tables and the 4 enum types exist. | `packages/api/tests/test_migration.py` |
| 2 | Run `alembic downgrade base`, then `alembic upgrade head`. | Both commands succeed. No table or enum type is left after the downgrade. | `packages/api/tests/test_migration.py` |
| 3 | Run `uv run mc-seed` two times against `mc_test` as a subprocess. | Both runs exit with 0. The row counts per table are equal after each run. | `packages/api/tests/test_seed.py` |
| 4 | Query the seeded data with SQL. | The counts of AC9, the rules of AC10 and the scenarios of AC11 to AC13 are true. | `packages/api/tests/test_seed.py` |
| 5 | Read the README run steps and the user table. | The steps contain `uv run mc-seed`. The table lists each seeded username. | manual: the README content is prose. A test cannot judge that it is clear. |

| Question | Answer | Source |

| Task name and folder | `data-model-seed`, `.work/data-model-seed/` | me |
| How do the tests isolate their data? | A separate database `mc_test`. The test session creates and migrates it. Each test rolls back its transaction. | me |
| How does the reviewer load the seed? | A Python seed command `uv run mc-seed`, after `alembic upgrade head`. It deletes the existing data and inserts the seed again. | me |
| Which dates does the seed use? | Fixed dates, in the period November 2026 to March 2027. | me |
| How does the DB store the enums? | Native Postgres ENUM types. | me |
| Which values does `unavailability.reason` have? | `HOLIDAY`, `SICK`, `MEETING` only. | me |
| What is the E2E check of step 2? | An integration test runs the seed command against the test DB and checks the data with SQL. verify:full runs it with pytest. | me |
| Which build approach? | SQLAlchemy models, an autogenerated Alembic migration, a Python seed module with ORM objects. | me |
| Which table names? | `organization` and `app_user`. The other tables use the singular names of the design: `skill`, `crew_skill`, `unavailability`, `mission`, `mission_requirement`, `assignment`. | me |
| Does `crew_skill` have an `id` column? | No. The PK is `(user_id, skill_id)`. | `design/DESIGN.md:171` |
| Which values do the other enums have? | `user_role`: DIRECTOR, LEAD, CREW. `mission_status`: DRAFT, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, APPROVED, ACTIVE, COMPLETED, CANCELLED. `assignment_status`: INVITED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, CANCELLED. | `design/DESIGN.md:149`, `:194`, `:227` |
| Schema details: Python UUIDs, server default timestamps, ORM `updated_at`, naming convention, no relationships, manual enum drop in the downgrade | Approved as design section 1. | me |
| Which tables have the cross-org foreign keys? | The 7 rows of the composite foreign key table. | `design/DESIGN.md:363-371` |
| What is the workload window? | A code constant, example 90 days. The seed places the workload within 60 days of the reference window, so it counts for each window of 60 days or more. | `design/DESIGN.md:239` |
| Where is the run command? | The CLAUDE.md "Run locally" line and the README run steps. Both get the seed step. | `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md:12-18` |

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.

**When no execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**

- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
- **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.

**For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**

**When an execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

**If Subagent-driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

**If Native chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans

# Data Model and Seed Implementation Plan

> Run with /implement-plan /Users/janeshorst/Dev/mutinex-interview/.work/data-model-seed/plan.md in a fresh context.

**Goal:** Add the P0 schema with tenant-safe composite foreign keys, the first Alembic migration and the `mc-seed` demo data command.

**Architecture:** SQLAlchemy 2 models in `mc_api.models` define the 8 tables on the existing `Base`. Alembic autogenerates one migration from the models. `mc_api.seed` deletes all rows and inserts one fixed dataset in one transaction. The tests run against a separate database `mc_test`.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, SQLAlchemy 2.1.4, Alembic 1.20.0, psycopg 3.3.6, Postgres 17, pytest 9.1.1 (versions from `uv.lock`).

**Spec:** /Users/janeshorst/Dev/mutinex-interview/.work/data-model-seed/spec.md
**Verify:** verify:full = `.claude/hooks/verify.sh full`; verify:fast = `.claude/hooks/verify.sh fast`
**Contract:** Covers, Tests must prove, Files, Interfaces, Global Constraints and Checkpoint are binding. Report each change to them to the human. The implementer chooses the code.

## Global Constraints

- Add no new dependency. All needed packages are in `packages/api/pyproject.toml:5-12` and the dev group in `pyproject.toml:18-19`.
- Table names: `organization`, `app_user`, `skill`, `crew_skill`, `unavailability`, `mission`, `mission_requirement`, `assignment`.
- Native Postgres enum types: `user_role` (DIRECTOR, LEAD, CREW), `mission_status` (DRAFT, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, APPROVED, ACTIVE, COMPLETED, CANCELLED), `assignment_status` (INVITED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, CANCELLED), `unavailability_reason` (HOLIDAY, SICK, MEETING).
- Column names and types follow `design/DESIGN.md:133-232` exactly. Add no P1 column (`mission_seq`, `number`, `slug`).
- Each tenant table has `org_id NOT NULL` with an FK to `organization`. The composite FKs follow `design/DESIGN.md:363-371`.
- Each table has a UUID `id` PK, except `crew_skill` (PK `(user_id, skill_id)`, `design/DESIGN.md:171`). Each table has `created_at` and `updated_at` (`timestamptz`).
- Foreign keys use the default `ON DELETE NO ACTION`. No cascade delete.
- Do not change `mc_shared`. Add no API endpoint and no CLI command.
- Seed dates are fixed. Missions and leave are in November 2026 to March 2027. Only the COMPLETED mission is in September 2026. Each timestamp (`approved_at`, `responded_at`) is before 2026-10-11 and has the UTC time zone.
- The test database is `mc_test` on the server of `DATABASE_URL`. No test writes to the dev database `mc`.
- Run Alembic from the repo root (`alembic.ini:2`). Ruff line length is 100 (`pyproject.toml:25`).
- Do not edit `BRIEF.md`. Write README and CLAUDE.md text in Simplified Technical English.

## Review Focus

1. A reviewer runs `mc-seed` before `alembic upgrade head`. Expected: exit code 1 and a message that names `uv run alembic upgrade head`. No traceback. Slice 2 tests it.
2. A reviewer runs `mc-seed` while Postgres is down. Expected: exit code 1 and a message that names `docker compose up -d`. No traceback and no password in the output. Slice 2 tests it.
3. A developer runs `uv run pytest` a second time, or after an aborted run left rows in `mc_test`. Expected: all tests pass again. No test assumes empty tables. The checkpoint of each slice runs the suite two times.
4. A later step deletes a user or a mission that has children. Expected: the DB rejects the delete, so assignment history is never lost silently (`design/DESIGN.md:240`). Slice 1 tests it.

I checked the spec for a fifth input class. I found none that a test of this step can exercise.

---

### Slice 1: The migration creates the tenant-safe schema, and the tests use `mc_test`

**Files:**
- Modify: `packages/api/src/mc_api/db.py:13-14` (naming convention on `Base.metadata`)
- Create: `packages/api/src/mc_api/models.py`
- Modify: `packages/api/alembic/env.py:5` (import the models)
- Create: `packages/api/alembic/versions/<rev>_add_data_model.py` (autogenerated)
- Test (test writer): `packages/api/tests/conftest.py`, `packages/api/tests/test_migration.py`, `packages/api/tests/test_schema.py`

**Covers:** AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC14

**Tests must prove:** The migration creates the 8 tables and the 4 enums, and the downgrade removes them. The DB rejects cross-org links, bad values and duplicate keys. The timestamps work. The tests never write to `mc`. Examples:
- E2E: `alembic upgrade head` on `mc_test` → the 8 tables exist. `pg_enum` lists the 4 types with the exact values of Global Constraints.
- E2E: `alembic downgrade base` → none of the 8 tables and none of the 4 enum types exist. Then `alembic upgrade head` → succeeds.
- integration: `alembic.command.check` on `mc_test` at head → no `AutogenerateDiffsDetected`.
- integration: for each of the 10 links of `design/DESIGN.md:363-371`, an insert that references a row of org B from a row of org A → `IntegrityError`. The links are: assignment→mission, assignment→app_user, assignment→mission_requirement, mission_requirement→mission, mission_requirement→skill, crew_skill→app_user, crew_skill→skill, unavailability→app_user, mission.lead_id→app_user, mission.approved_by→app_user.
- integration: the same insert with rows of one org → succeeds.
- integration: `org_id` NULL on each of the 7 tenant tables → `IntegrityError`.
- integration: assignment with `mission_id` of mission A and `requirement_id` of a slot of mission B, same org → `IntegrityError`.
- integration: `crew_skill.level` 0 or 6 → `IntegrityError`. Level 1 and 5 → succeed. The same for `mission_requirement.min_level`.
- integration: `unavailability` and `mission` with `end_date` one day before `start_date` → `IntegrityError`. `end_date == start_date` → succeeds.
- integration: second user `ava` in another org → `IntegrityError`. Skill "EVA" two times in org A → `IntegrityError`. Skill "EVA" in org A and in org B → succeeds.
- integration: two active slots with position 1 in one mission → `IntegrityError`. Slot 1 archived (`archived_at` set), new slot with position 1 → succeeds.
- integration: second INVITED assignment for the same mission and user → `IntegrityError`. Second INVITED assignment for the same slot → `IntegrityError`. The first one DECLINED, then a new INVITED for the same slot and user → succeeds. The same with CANCELLED.
- integration: insert a mission → `created_at` and `updated_at` are set. Change its title and flush → `updated_at` is later than before, `created_at` is the same.
- integration: delete an `app_user` that has a `crew_skill` → `IntegrityError`. Delete a `mission` that has an `assignment` → `IntegrityError`.
- integration: `mc_api.db.engine.url.database == "mc_test"`.
- integration: a session fixture counts the rows of each existing table in `mc` at the start and at the end of the run → the counts are equal.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `mc_api.db.Base`, `engine`, `SessionLocal`, `DATABASE_URL` (`packages/api/src/mc_api/db.py:7-14`). `db.py` reads `DATABASE_URL` at import time, so the conftest must set the variable before it imports `mc_api`.
- Produces, in `mc_api.models`:
  - `StrEnum` classes `UserRole`, `MissionStatus`, `AssignmentStatus`, `UnavailabilityReason`. The member names are equal to the values.
  - Models `Organization`, `AppUser`, `Skill`, `CrewSkill`, `Unavailability`, `Mission`, `MissionRequirement`, `Assignment`. The attribute names are the column names of `design/DESIGN.md:133-232`. Example: `AppUser.username`, `Mission.lead_id`, `MissionRequirement.archived_at`, `Assignment.responded_at`.
  - No ORM relationships.
- Produces, in `packages/api/tests/conftest.py` (test writer): a `session` fixture that wraps each test in a transaction and rolls it back, and an `alembic_cfg` fixture.

**Steps:**

- [ ] **Step 1 (test writer): Write the conftest.**
  At import time, keep the dev URL and set `os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]` to the same URL with database `mc_test`. Use `sqlalchemy.engine.make_url(...).set(database="mc_test")`. The default URL is `postgresql+psycopg://mc:mc@localhost:5432/mc` (`packages/api/src/mc_api/db.py:7`).
  In a session fixture, connect to the dev database with `AUTOCOMMIT`, and create `mc_test` if `pg_database` does not have it. Then run `alembic.command.upgrade(cfg, "head")`. Build `cfg` from the absolute path of `alembic.ini`.
  The `session` fixture opens a connection on `mc_api.db.engine`, begins a transaction, and binds a `Session` with `join_transaction_mode="create_savepoint"`. It rolls back at teardown.
  Add the dev-count fixture of the last example as an autouse session fixture. It counts only the tables that exist in `mc`.
  The subprocess tests of slice 2 inherit `DATABASE_URL=mc_test` from this environment.

- [ ] **Step 2 (test writer): Write `test_migration.py` and `test_schema.py`** with the examples above.
  The round-trip test must end at `head`, so later tests have the schema.
  The tests must not assume empty tables (Review Focus 3). Make each test create its own orgs, with unique usernames such as `f"ava-{uuid4()}"`.
  To test more than one failing insert in a test, run each insert in `session.begin_nested()`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Run the new tests and see them fail.**
  Run: `uv run pytest packages/api/tests -q`
  Expected: FAIL. `test_schema.py` cannot import `mc_api.models`. `test_health.py` passes against `mc_test`.

- [ ] **Step 4 (implementer): Add a naming convention to `Base.metadata`** in `db.py`. Alembic needs known names to drop a constraint in a later migration. SQLAlchemy 2.1.4 shortens names longer than 63 characters with a hash suffix (checked in this session).

  ```python
  NAMING_CONVENTION = {
      "ix": "ix_%(column_0_N_label)s",
      "uq": "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_N_name)s",
      "ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
      "fk": "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_N_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
      "pk": "pk_%(table_name)s",
  }
  ```

  Give each `CheckConstraint` a short name, for example `level_range` or `dates`. The `ck` convention needs it.

- [ ] **Step 5 (implementer): Write `models.py`.** Use these columns. The column types are: `uuid` = `Uuid`, `text` = `Text`, `date` = `Date`, `timestamptz` = `DateTime(timezone=True)`, `smallint` = `SmallInteger`.

  | Model | Columns | Table constraints |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Organization` | `id`, `name text` | — |
  | `AppUser` | `id`, `org_id`, `username text`, `display_name text`, `role user_role` | `UNIQUE(username)`, `UNIQUE(org_id, id)` |
  | `Skill` | `id`, `org_id`, `name text`, `description text NULL` | `UNIQUE(org_id, name)`, `UNIQUE(org_id, id)` |
  | `CrewSkill` | `org_id`, `user_id`, `skill_id`, `level smallint` | PK `(user_id, skill_id)`. FK `(org_id, user_id)` → `app_user(org_id, id)`. FK `(org_id, skill_id)` → `skill(org_id, id)`. `CHECK level BETWEEN 1 AND 5` |
  | `Unavailability` | `id`, `org_id`, `user_id`, `start_date date`, `end_date date`, `reason unavailability_reason` | FK `(org_id, user_id)` → `app_user`. `CHECK end_date >= start_date` |
  | `Mission` | `id`, `org_id`, `title text`, `description text NULL`, `lead_id`, `status mission_status`, `start_date date`, `end_date date`, `approved_by NULL`, `approved_at timestamptz NULL` | `UNIQUE(org_id, id)`. FK `(org_id, lead_id)` → `app_user`. FK `(org_id, approved_by)` → `app_user`. `CHECK end_date >= start_date` |
  | `MissionRequirement` | `id`, `org_id`, `mission_id`, `position smallint`, `skill_id`, `min_level smallint`, `archived_at timestamptz NULL` | `UNIQUE(org_id, mission_id, id)`. FK `(org_id, mission_id)` → `mission`. FK `(org_id, skill_id)` → `skill`. `CHECK min_level BETWEEN 1 AND 5`. Unique index `(mission_id, position) WHERE archived_at IS NULL` |
  | `Assignment` | `id`, `org_id`, `mission_id`, `requirement_id`, `user_id`, `status assignment_status`, `responded_at timestamptz NULL` | FK `(org_id, mission_id)` → `mission`. FK `(org_id, mission_id, requirement_id)` → `mission_requirement(org_id, mission_id, id)`. FK `(org_id, user_id)` → `app_user`. Unique index `(mission_id, user_id) WHERE status IN ('INVITED','ACCEPTED')`. Unique index `(requirement_id) WHERE status IN ('INVITED','ACCEPTED')` |

  - Each column is `NOT NULL` unless the table says `NULL`. Each `org_id` also has an FK to `organization.id`.
  - `id` uses `default=uuid.uuid4`.
  - Put `created_at` and `updated_at` in one mixin. Both use `server_default=func.now()`. `updated_at` also uses `onupdate=func.clock_timestamp()`. Reason: `now()` returns the start time of the transaction, so an update in the same transaction does not change the value.
  - Use `postgresql_where` for the partial unique indexes. Give the enums their names with `Enum(UserRole, name="user_role")`.

- [ ] **Step 6 (implementer): Import the models in `env.py`** after the `mc_api.db` import. Use `import mc_api.models  # noqa: F401`. Without it, `Base.metadata` is empty and autogenerate finds no tables.

- [ ] **Step 7 (implementer): Generate the migration.**
  Make sure that the dev database `mc` has no tables and no `alembic_version` row. Autogenerate compares the models with that database.
  Run: `docker compose up -d && uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m "add data model"`
  Read the file. Check that it creates the 4 enum types, the 8 tables, the named constraints and the 3 partial indexes with `postgresql_where`.
  Check the downgrade. If it does not drop the 4 enum types, add a drop for each type after the `drop_table` calls. Use `sa.Enum(name="user_role").drop(op.get_bind(), checkfirst=True)`, and the same for the 3 other types.
  Run: `uv run alembic upgrade head`. Expected: success on the dev database.

- [ ] **Step 8: Run the tests and see them pass.**
  Run: `uv run pytest packages/api/tests -q`
  Expected: PASS.

**Checkpoint:** `.claude/hooks/verify.sh full` → exit 0, no `ERROR` line. Run it a second time → exit 0 again (Review Focus 3). `test_migration.py` is the E2E test of this slice.

---

### Slice 2: `mc-seed` loads the demo dataset

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/api/src/mc_api/seed.py`
- Modify: `packages/api/pyproject.toml` (add `[project.scripts]`)
- Modify: `README.md:12-18` (run steps), `README.md:28-32` (test section), add a "Seed data" section
- Modify: `CLAUDE.md` ("Run locally" line in "Commands")
- Test (test writer): `packages/api/tests/test_seed.py`

**Covers:** AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11, AC12, AC13, AC15

**Tests must prove:** The command loads the dataset again on each run. The data has the orgs, the roles, the rules and the matcher scenarios of the spec. The command fails clearly without a schema or without Postgres. Examples:
- E2E: `uv run mc-seed` two times as a subprocess, with `DATABASE_URL` for `mc_test` → exit 0 both times. The row count of each of the 8 tables and the set of usernames are equal after run 1 and run 2.

- E2E: `uv run mc-seed` with `DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://mc:secret@localhost:1/mc` → exit 1. The output contains `docker compose up -d`, no `Traceback` and no `secret`.
- integration (AC9): org A has 2 DIRECTOR, 2 LEAD and 8 or more CREW users. Org B has 1 DIRECTOR, 1 LEAD and 3 or more CREW users. A skill name exists in both orgs, with two different `id` values.
- integration (AC10): each of these SQL queries returns 0 rows:
  - a `crew_skill` or `assignment` row whose user is not CREW;
  - a mission whose lead is not LEAD or DIRECTOR;
  - a mission with `approved_by` whose approver is not DIRECTOR or is the lead;

# Data Model and Seed Implementation Plan

> Run with /implement-plan /Users/janeshorst/Dev/mutinex-interview/.work/data-model-seed/plan.md in a fresh context.

**Goal:** Add the P0 schema with tenant-safe composite foreign keys, the first Alembic migration and the `mc-seed` demo data command.

**Architecture:** SQLAlchemy 2 models in `mc_api.models` define the 8 tables on the existing `Base`. Alembic autogenerates one migration from the models. `mc_api.seed` deletes all rows and inserts one fixed dataset in one transaction. The tests run against a separate database `mc_test`.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, SQLAlchemy 2.1.4, Alembic 1.20.0, psycopg 3.3.6, Postgres 17, pytest 9.1.1 (versions from `uv.lock`).

**Spec:** /Users/janeshorst/Dev/mutinex-interview/.work/data-model-seed/spec.md
**Verify:** verify:full = `.claude/hooks/verify.sh full`; verify:fast = `.claude/hooks/verify.sh fast`
**Contract:** Covers, Tests must prove, Files, Interfaces, Global Constraints and Checkpoint are binding. Report each change to them to the human. The implementer chooses the code.

## Global Constraints

- Add no new dependency. All needed packages are in `packages/api/pyproject.toml:5-12` and the dev group in `pyproject.toml:18-19`.
- Table names: `organization`, `app_user`, `skill`, `crew_skill`, `unavailability`, `mission`, `mission_requirement`, `assignment`.
- Native Postgres enum types: `user_role` (DIRECTOR, LEAD, CREW), `mission_status` (DRAFT, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, APPROVED, ACTIVE, COMPLETED, CANCELLED), `assignment_status` (INVITED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, CANCELLED), `unavailability_reason` (HOLIDAY, SICK, MEETING).
- Column names and types follow `design/DESIGN.md:133-232` exactly. Add no P1 column (`mission_seq`, `number`, `slug`).
- Each tenant table has `org_id NOT NULL` with an FK to `organization`. The composite FKs follow `design/DESIGN.md:363-371`.
- Each table has a UUID `id` PK, except `crew_skill` (PK `(user_id, skill_id)`, `design/DESIGN.md:171`). Each table has `created_at` and `updated_at` (`timestamptz`).
- Foreign keys use the default `ON DELETE NO ACTION`. No cascade delete.
- Do not change `mc_shared`. Add no API endpoint and no CLI command.
- Seed dates are fixed. Missions and leave are in November 2026 to March 2027. Only the COMPLETED mission is in September 2026. Each timestamp (`approved_at`, `responded_at`) is before 2026-10-11 and has the UTC time zone.
- The test database is `mc_test` on the server of `DATABASE_URL`. No test writes to the dev database `mc`.
- Run Alembic from the repo root (`alembic.ini:2`). Ruff line length is 100 (`pyproject.toml:25`).

## Review Focus

1. A reviewer runs `mc-seed` before `alembic upgrade head`. Expected: exit code 1 and a message that names `uv run alembic upgrade head`. No traceback. Slice 2 tests it.
2. A reviewer runs `mc-seed` while Postgres is down. Expected: exit code 1 and a message that names `docker compose up -d`. No traceback and no password in the output. Slice 2 tests it.
3. A developer runs `uv run pytest` a second time, or after an aborted run left rows in `mc_test`. Expected: all tests pass again. No test assumes empty tables. The checkpoint of each slice runs the suite two times.
4. A later step deletes a user or a mission that has children. Expected: the DB rejects the delete, so assignment history is never lost silently (`design/DESIGN.md:240`). Slice 1 tests it.

**Architecture:** SQLAlchemy 2 models in `mc_api.models` define the 8 tables on the existing `Base`. Alembic autogenerates one migration from the models. `mc_api.seed` deletes all rows and inserts one fixed dataset in one transaction. The tests run against a separate database `mc_test`.

- Slots: partial unique index on assignment (requirement_id) WHERE status IN (INVITED, ACCEPTED): one active assignment per slot

# Spec: data-model-seed

## Goal
Add the P0 data model, the first Alembic migration and a demo seed command (build step 2, `design/DESIGN.md:65`).
The schema enforces tenant isolation for writes with composite foreign keys. The seed data shows the matcher trade-offs that later steps demonstrate.

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | The tests must prove |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | `uv run alembic upgrade head` on an empty database creates the 8 tables and the 4 native enum types. (DESIGN Data model, `design/DESIGN.md:121-232`) | After the upgrade, the tables `organization`, `app_user`, `skill`, `crew_skill`, `unavailability`, `mission`, `mission_requirement`, `assignment` exist. The enum types `user_role`, `mission_status`, `assignment_status`, `unavailability_reason` exist with the values of the design. |
| AC2 | The migration and the models agree, and the downgrade is complete. | `alembic check` reports no difference. A downgrade to `base` removes all 8 tables and all 4 enum types. A second upgrade then succeeds. |
| AC3 | Each tenant table has `org_id NOT NULL`. The DB rejects each cross-org link of the composite foreign key table. (P0 req 4, `design/DESIGN.md:357-371`) | For each row of `design/DESIGN.md:363-371`, an insert that links rows of two different orgs fails with an integrity error. The same insert with rows of one org succeeds. An insert with `org_id` NULL fails. |
| AC4 | An assignment can reference only a slot of its own mission. (`design/DESIGN.md:225`) | An assignment with `mission_id` of mission A and `requirement_id` of a slot of mission B in the same org fails. |
| AC5 | The DB enforces the value checks. (`design/DESIGN.md:169`, `:182`, `:196`, `:211`) | `crew_skill.level` and `mission_requirement.min_level` reject 0 and 6, and accept 1 and 5. `unavailability` and `mission` reject `end_date` before `start_date`, and accept `end_date` equal to `start_date`. |
| AC6 | The DB enforces the unique keys. (`design/DESIGN.md:147`, `:158`, `:209`, `:230-231`) | A second user with the same `username` fails, also in another org. A second skill with the same name fails in one org and succeeds in another org. A second active slot with the same position in one mission fails. A new slot can use the position of an archived slot. A second INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment for the same mission and user fails. A second INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment for the same slot fails. A new INVITED assignment succeeds after the earlier one is DECLINED or CANCELLED. |
| AC7 | Each table has `created_at` and `updated_at`. (`design/DESIGN.md:130`) | An insert sets both values. An ORM update of a row changes `updated_at` and keeps `created_at`. |
| AC8 | `uv run mc-seed` loads the demo dataset into a migrated database. A second run gives the same state. (P0 req 1, req 3) | The command exits with 0. After two runs, the row count of each table is the same as after one run, and the usernames are the same. |
| AC9 | The seed has 2 orgs. Org A has 2 directors, 2 leads and at least 8 crew members. Org B has 1 director, 1 lead and at least 3 crew members. (P0 req 3) | The counts of users per org and role match. Each org has its own skill catalogue. At least one skill name exists in both orgs as two different rows. |
| AC10 | The seed data obeys the service rules that the DB does not enforce. (`design/DESIGN.md:172`, `:193`, `:226`, `:338-345`) | Each `crew_skill` user and each `assignment` user has the role CREW. Each mission lead has the role LEAD or DIRECTOR. Each mission with `approved_by` has an approver with the role DIRECTOR who is not the lead. Each mission in APPROVED or COMPLETED has `approved_by` and `approved_at`. Assignments exist only on missions in APPROVED or COMPLETED. No crew member has two INVITED or ACCEPTED assignments on missions with overlapping dates. Each assigned crew member has the slot skill at the minimum level or higher. |
| AC11 | The seed shows the matcher trade-offs for a reference window in org A: 2027-01-11 to 2027-01-24, slots Piloting ≥ 3, EVA ≥ 3, Medicine ≥ 2. (P0 req 3, `design/DESIGN.md:389-399`) | Expert against closest fit: two crew members have Piloting, one at level 5 and one at level 3. Leave: a crew member with EVA ≥ 3 has unavailability that overlaps the window. Booking: a crew member with Medicine ≥ 2 has an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment on a mission that overlaps the window. Workload: two crew members have EVA at the same level ≥ 3 and are free in the window. One has INVITED or ACCEPTED mission days within 60 days of the window, and the other has none. |
| AC12 | The seed has assignment history for crew members. (P0 req 14) | At least one assignment is DECLINED. At least one ACCEPTED assignment is on a COMPLETED mission. The COMPLETED mission ends before 2026-10-11. |
| AC13 | Org B has a target of each type for the cross-org checks of later steps. (P0 req 22) | Org B has at least one skill, crew skill, unavailability, mission, slot and assignment. |
| AC14 | `uv run pytest` uses a separate database `mc_test`. The dev database keeps its data. | After a full test run, the row counts in the dev database `mc` are the same as before the run. The test session creates `mc_test` if it does not exist and migrates it to `head`. |
| AC15 | The README tells the reviewer how to seed the data and which users exist. (P0 req 1) | Manual review: the README run steps and the CLAUDE.md "Run locally" line contain `uv run mc-seed` after `alembic upgrade head`. The README has a table of the seeded usernames with org and role. The README says that `mc-seed` deletes all data in the database of `DATABASE_URL`. |

## Non-goals
- No API endpoints and no CLI commands for the data. Steps 3 to 9 add them.
- No shared Pydantic types in `mc_shared`. No API response uses the models yet.
- No org-scoped data-access layer, no login and no JWT. Step 3 adds them.
- No matcher code. The seed only provides the data for the matcher scenarios of step 5.
- No ORM relationships between the models. A later step adds a relationship when a query needs it.
- No P1 columns: no `mission_seq`, no mission `number`, no skill `slug`.
- No docker-compose service for the seed.

## End-to-end check
| # | Action | Expected result | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Run `alembic upgrade head` on the empty `mc_test` database. | The 8 tables and the 4 enum types exist. | `packages/api/tests/test_migration.py` |
| 2 | Run `alembic downgrade base`, then `alembic upgrade head`. | Both commands succeed. No table or enum type is left after the downgrade. | `packages/api/tests/test_migration.py` |
| 3 | Run `uv run mc-seed` two times against `mc_test` as a subprocess. | Both runs exit with 0. The row counts per table are equal after each run. | `packages/api/tests/test_seed.py` |
| 4 | Query the seeded data with SQL. | The counts of AC9, the rules of AC10 and the scenarios of AC11 to AC13 are true. | `packages/api/tests/test_seed.py` |
| 5 | Read the README, the CLAUDE.md run line and the user table. | The run steps contain `uv run mc-seed`. The table lists each seeded username. The README gives the data loss warning. | manual: the README content is prose. A test cannot judge that it is clear. |

## Resolved questions

|---|---|---|

| Which dates does the seed use? | Fixed dates, in the period November 2026 to March 2027. | me |

| What are the seed size and the reference window? | As AC9 and AC11 give them. | me |

| Which build approach? | SQLAlchemy models, an autogenerated Alembic migration, a Python seed module with ORM objects. | me |
| Which table names? | `organization` and `app_user`. The other tables use the singular names of the design: `skill`, `crew_skill`, `unavailability`, `mission`, `mission_requirement`, `assignment`. | me |

| Which values do the other enums have? | `user_role`: DIRECTOR, LEAD, CREW. `mission_status`: DRAFT, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, APPROVED, ACTIVE, COMPLETED, CANCELLED. `assignment_status`: INVITED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, CANCELLED. | `design/DESIGN.md:149`, `:194`, `:227` |

The check confirmed the enum-drop gap: Alembic's autogenerated downgrade leaves the enum types in the database. I ran the check in a temporary database `mc_spike` and dropped it after. I wrote nothing in the repo for it.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Autogenerated downgrade | It has only `drop_index` and `drop_table`. It does not drop the enum. |
| `op.drop_table` | The type `user_role` stays in the DB (count 1). |
| `sa.Enum(name="user_role").drop(...)` | The type is gone (count 0). |
| `compare_metadata` after create, with a partial unique index | `[]`, so `alembic check` raises no false alarm. |

**Changes:**
- `plan.md` slice 1, step 7: the downgrade fix is now a required step and cites this check. It also says that `alembic check` works with the partial indexes.
- `design/DECISIONS.md`, "Short references": a follow-up under the `username` bullet. Usernames are case-sensitive for now. A later fix is a unique index on `lower(username)` and a case-insensitive lookup in `mc login` and `--crew`.
- `spec.md`, "Resolved questions": a new row for the case-sensitive username, with source "me".

`DECISIONS.md` is a tracked file, and I did not commit the change. Commit it with build step 2, or in a separate commit.

**✋ Gate 2:** do you approve the plan at `/Users/janeshorst/Dev/mutinex-interview/.work/data-model-seed/plan.md`?

I ran the check on a small test model, not on the real 8-table models. So slice 1 must still read the generated migration file.
